newsitem.title: INDIA: India says weed in Australian wheat not harmful.
newsitem.headline: India says weed in Australian wheat not harmful.

text.p: Indian Agriculture Minister Chaturanan Mishra said on Tuesday that the "weed" detected in wheat import shipments from Australia was not harmful and common in wheat of any origin.
"We agree that weed was found in the imported shipments from Australia but it does not cause any health hazards and it is common in wheat of any origin," Mishra told reporters.
Mishra said India had taken precautionary steps to ensure that the weed infected wheat imports from Australia does not get diverted to wheat growing areas.
"We are trying to see that the wheat is not diverted to wheat growing areas," Mishra said.
In December, India authorised STC to import two million tonnes of wheat to build stocks and check rising prices.
STC officials have said they had so far contracted to import 1.75 million tonnes, mainly from Australia, Argentina and Canada. STC has said the entire quantity had already arrived at Indian ports.

On Monday, reports from Australia quoted Australian Wheat Board officials as saying that Australia had abided by all requirements in its wheat sales to India and had not received any official complaints about quality problems.
Officials said Australia, which has export contracts with India to a total of 2.325 million tonnes, had so far shipped 1.3 million.
